cues: To check the right piece has been cut or copied, run it on an agarose gel.
Load the samples in wells at the negative end.
DNA's phosphate groups make it negative at any pH, so every fragment moves towards the positive anode.
The gel is a sieve: short fragments slip through quickly and go far, long ones lag behind.
text: To check the right piece has been cut or copied, run it on an agarose gel. Load the samples in wells at the negative end. DNA's phosphate groups make it negative at any pH, so every fragment moves towards the positive anode. The gel is a sieve: short fragments slip through quickly and go far, long ones lag behind.
